title: ZTF confirms Gaia DR3 ellipsoidal amplitudes of 126 compact-companion candidates, but 40 have shapes outside a dark-companion Roche model and 29 of 30 with good parallax overfill the Roche lobe
abstract: Gaia DR3 lists 6,306 ellipsoidal variables that can have dark, massive companions. For 262 of them the one-sigma lower bound of the modified minimum mass ratio (mMMR) is more than 1. We fitted ZTF DR24 g and r light curves of 739 catalogue sources at the Gaia period: 126 high-confidence sources, 604 random comparison sources, and 14 systems that radial velocities already showed to have low-mass companions (Nagarajan et al. 2023). ZTF gives the Gaia double-wave period for 120 of 126 high-confidence sources, and the ZTF r to Gaia G amplitude ratio has a median of 1.01. Thus the large amplitudes are real and are not a Gaia sampling effect; with ZTF amplitudes, 117 of 126 keep mMMR > 1. We calculated 7,776 light curves per band of a Roche-distorted star with a dark point-mass companion (q = 0.5 to 20). In these models the cos(4 phi)/cos(2 phi) ratio is never above 0.086. The high-confidence group has an error-weighted mean ratio of 0.106 +/- 0.002, and 40 of 126 sources fail at least one shape test (2-sigma ratio rule or joint chi-square p < 0.001). Gaia GSP-Phot distances for these stars are about half the parallax distances, so we used parallax radii. If the companion is dark, 96% of 995 catalogue stars with parallax/error > 5 are larger than their Roche lobes (median R/R_L = 1.55); a conservative variant (lowest radius over all extinctions up to the SFD value, parallax +2 sigma, mass x1.5) gives 15%. The radius test flags 12 of 13 RV-rejected systems, but the shape test flags only 2 of 14, so a model-consistent shape is not evidence for a compact companion. The results agree with contact or near-contact binaries of two luminous stars for most candidates. One high-confidence source (Gaia DR3 1827494570016143232) passes both best-estimate tests at low parallax precision. Limitations: ZTF covers only declination > -30 deg, few candidates have precise parallaxes, the radius test depends on extinction and mass, and the Roche model has no spots.
